preview_pressure: The player must respect both a long Toxic clock and a fast sun opening.
primary_mode: Toxapex trapping clock backed by immediate mixed offense
secondary_mode: Charizard-Y sun and Choice Scarf Hydreigon burst
strategy_notes: Toxapex creates a trapping and Toxic clock while Charizard-Y, Hydreigon, and Sneasler prevent the team from becoming passive. Strong late Admin or boss template.

preview_pressure: Two visible Mega candidates conceal which defensive and speed profile the player will face.
secondary_mode: Conditional Steelix durability or Tyranitar sand setup
strategy_notes: Conditional Mega choice between Steelix board durability and Tyranitar setup pressure. Verdant must never activate both Megas in one battle.

preview_pressure: Party order can disguise Hisuian Zoroark as a materially different defensive target.
primary_mode: Illusion-backed special pressure under Tailwind or Icy Wind
strategy_notes: Party order and Illusion create the defining information puzzle. Fake Tears enables special burst while Dragonite supplies a separate priority endgame.

preview_pressure: The credible trap mode taxes preparation even when the AI chooses direct offense.
strategy_notes: Wolfe described Koraidon offense as the primary plan and Perish trapping as a credible secondary mode that taxes preparation even when unused.

preview_pressure: The same six threaten opposite speed orders.
primary_mode: Fast Koraidon and Flutter Mane sun pressure
secondary_mode: Lunala Trick Room into Guts Ursaluna
strategy_notes: Recent non-winning Wolfe team. Fast Koraidon and Flutter pressure transitions into Lunala and Guts Ursaluna Trick Room.

preview_pressure: Protecting safely against rain can expose the player to Encore plus Shadow Tag.
primary_mode: Politoed rain offense through Kingdra and Archaludon
strategy_notes: Politoed enables both direct Kingdra and Archaludon offense and the secondary Gothitelle Perish mode. Encore plus Shadow Tag punishes passive choices.

preview_pressure: An apparently slow Spore user changes speed behavior beside Galarian Weezing.
primary_mode: Neutralizing Gas enables fast Toedscruel disruption
secondary_mode: Scarf Eruption or Tailwind spread pressure
strategy_notes: Neutralizing Gas suppresses Mycelium Might and can make Toedscruel's Spore fast. The exact interaction must be tested in Verdant before reservation.

preview_pressure: Two Perish users and layered survival tools make the clock credible from several leads.
secondary_mode: Palafin and Flutter Mane direct cleanup
strategy_notes: Dedicated Perish mode with two singers and multiple survival tools. Reserve once for a late notorious trainer; ordinary damage AI is insufficient.

preview_pressure: Two Mega candidates and opposite speed modes make lead selection costly.
secondary_mode: Bronzong Trick Room with layered Fake Out, Nuzzle, Wide Guard, and Feint
strategy_notes: World-winning positioning team. Replace Primal Kyogre with base Kyogre; keep support interactions and conditional Mega choice under explicit AI control.

preview_pressure: Multiple activation partners obscure when Coalossal will accelerate.
primary_mode: Partner self-activation of Steam Engine and Weakness Policy
secondary_mode: Alternate offensive partner prevents one-dimensional targeting
strategy_notes: Dragapult Surf or Urshifu Aqua Jet activates Steam Engine and Weakness Policy. Gigantamax residual damage is unavailable, so Verdant should import the activation core rather than pretend the full win condition survives.
Current Mega-era championship anchor with two selectable Megas, field control, and a Last Respects endgame.
Three coherent modes: sun offense, fast Scarf Garchomp, or Sinistcha Trick Room into bulky Mega Floette.
Alternative-Mega team with Gengar control and independent Kommo-o and Kingambit setup endgames.
Tempo control through layered priority, Fake Out, pivots, Icy Wind, and Thunder Wave rather than a conventional speed setter.
Manual-sun TailRoom offense with anti-Protect and priority-denial layers.
Fast Koraidon, Chi-Yu, and Flutter mode transitions into Lunala Trick Room and Guts Ursaluna.
Specs Miraidon and Tailwind on one axis, Electric Seed Lunala and Ursaluna Trick Room on the other.
A genuine fast/slow terrain hybrid rather than a single setter-and-sweeper module.
Difficulty comes from pure board positioning rather than a visible speed setter. Valuable anti-formula boss reference.
Definitive CHALK balance. Swagger-heavy adaptation should preserve strategy without making variance the primary difficulty source.
Canonical proof that an apparently weak support Pokémon can define an elite encounter.
Fast conventional offense plus a dangerous self-Swagger slow mode. Gems can be replaced while preserving the structure.
